heading: The fourteenth day of October, in the seventh year of Kunrad IV. Third desk, second floor. Four dockets in the passage.
burnt_out_text: The second candle drowned with dockets still in the tray. The doorkeeper copied their names into tomorrow's passage list.

document.title: Memorandum on a Foreign Reckoning
document.body:
It is reported that this desk admitted the Saint Wend instrument for Kesselholt by election reckoning.

The Chancery records regnal years from accession. A notary may choose to serve another authority, but he may not call that choice Imperial law. Enter the positions distinctly in the Register and be prepared to account for the consequence.
document.closing: The eagle has not changed the year from which it counts.

document.title: Notice of Appeal from Saint Wend
document.sender: The Cathedral Chapter of Saint Wend
document.recipient: The notary of the third desk
document.body:
Your denial of the Kesselholt grant has been entered before the Bishop's court.

The instrument was drawn by our chancery and dated according to the election from which we count. The Church does not accept that a later Imperial habit can make an earlier episcopal act impossible. The abbey's cutters remain under our protection pending appeal.
document.closing: What your office refused, our law continues to admit.

document.title: Joint Covering Sheet — Kesselholt
document.recipient: The third desk, for immediate return
document.body:
The referred instrument has arrived under both seals.

The Imperial Chancery requires the wood secured while accession reckoning is examined. The Chapter of Saint Wend requires felling to continue while election reckoning is defended.

Both offices direct this desk to move the matter without delay. Neither agrees what movement means.
document.closing: Two endorsements do not make one command.

opening_documents._note: THURSDAY ANSWERS FOR THE KNIFE. Until now every one of this day's arrivals gated on case_03, and case_08 -- Tuesday's deliberate sting in the tail, the matter the day file itself calls the day's sting -- produced no Thursday consequence whatever. The player's worst available ruling was one skippable paragraph in the ledger and then Thursday simply began. The CONFIRM branch returns the instrument itself, with the wax cut off and every erasure at the same fraction of the same sheet, and asks nothing. There is no ring for it. The player spends Thursday morning holding the parchment they got wrong into their own candle, alone, and finds it in about four seconds.

document.title: Writ of Recall
document.body:
The instrument for the mill upon the Aue, admitted at this desk on Tuesday, is recalled.

The Duke's chancery is asked how a grant of the eighth year binds portions settled in the ninth, and answers that it does not, and never did. The year on the parchment is not the year the parchment was written.

The wax has been cut from the cord and filed with the office copy. The instrument itself is returned to this desk. No ruling is required of you. Read it again.
document.closing: Nothing is asked. The file is closed either way.

document.title: Returned instrument: the mill upon the Aue
document.body_text:
Berthold, by the grace of God Duke of Ostmark, to all who shall see this writing, greeting.

Know that we have granted to Reimbold Zant and to his heirs the mill upon the Aue below Tanneck with the two meadows above the race, to hold of us for the yearly render of six measures of meal.

And we will that this grant bind our inheritance whole, and every portion of it hereafter.

In witness whereof we have set our seal.
document.claimant: Reimbold Zant, miller, and his heirs
document.property: The mill upon the Aue below Tanneck, with the two meadows above the race

witnesses.name: Hartwig vom Aue
witnesses.title: forester of the Duke on the Aue

witnesses.name: Egilbert Roth
witnesses.title: chaplain of the Duke's chapel at Tanneck

erasures.original_value: in the eleventh year of Aldric I

erasures.altered_field: The style given to the second witness
erasures.note: Ostmark keeps no sworn measurers; that is a Marchfeld office, and the man is a Marchfeld man. The scribe gave him the wrong style, saw it, and set it right while the ink of the rest was still wet.

document.title: Office Receipt
document.body:
Received of the third desk, one refused instrument for the mill upon the Aue, entered as false in the year.

The party has been written to. He denies the knife and offers the names of two men who saw the grant made, one of whom is the forester who witnessed it.

The office has not asked him for a third.
document.closing: Filed. Two marks for the writing, not received of the party.

document.title: Note of Position
document.body:
The instrument for the mill upon the Aue stands referred.

It is eleventh in the order and has not been opened. The party has written twice to ask which of the two questions is being considered, and has been told that the file is with the Vice-Chancellor.

The file is not with the Vice-Chancellor.
document.closing: Position unchanged. Entered for the record, which is the whole of what a note of position is for.
